fatal_blockers: Proposal 1 has not shown that bounded-sum-free fingerprints are compatible with one fixed, assignment-independent target for all honest encodings. Construction A amplifies only nonzero syndromes; any prescribed-coset collision remains an exact kernel, and constant h gives no asymptotic protection against larger signed combinations.

Proposal 2 is killed as stated. In a bounded-degree complex, the boundary and coboundary of a constant-support defect have only constant support, while integral cocycles remain exact zero-syndrome attacks; no concrete complex or expansion theorem is supplied.

Proposal 3 is killed by signed transportation circulations. Any zero-mass selector deviation can be lifted on each incident edge by a constant-support 2-by-2 transportation move with zero opposite projection, so bounded-degree expander edges do not force propagation.

Proposal 4 is killed as an independent mechanism. The product formula only lower-bounds a nonzero algebraic syndrome, which ordinary weighted integer rows already do; it neither excludes exact kernels nor proves compatibility between algebraic independence and equal completeness radius.

Proposal 5 is killed in this form because exact base kernels survive tensoring, and no fixed-target walk tensor or valid multiplicativity inequality is defined. A k=2 numerical ratio cannot overcome that structural blocker or justify logarithmic powering.

Proposal 6 is killed as a route to the target absent a uniform polynomial degree and coefficient bound. A certificate computation on the nine-clause instance cannot address general formulas, and faithful conversion of the Macaulay pairing into an emitted fixed-target CVP lattice is unproved.
